topic: Atmospheric Geochemistry: Diatomic Oxygen Abundance
question: What percentage of the earth’s atmosphere does O,, comprise ? :
correct_text: 21% (Dry atmospheric air is composed of 78.08% nitrogen (N2), 20.95% (~21%) oxygen (O2), 0.93% argon (Ar), and 0.04% carbon dioxide (CO2))

topic: Atmospheric Science: Major Atmospheric Constituent
question: Which gas makes the majority of our _ atmosphere ? _ “=
correct_text: Nitrogen (Nitrogen gas (N2) is the predominant gas in the Earth's atmosphere, constituting 78.08% of dry air by volume)
textbook_ref: Edward A. Keller (Environmental Geology, Ch. 2); Arthur N. Strahler (Physical Geography, Ch. 4)

topic: Marine Geohazards: Seismically Triggered Tsunami Waves
question: Wave generated by underwater . earthquakes is called : . . -
correct_text: Tsunami (Large ocean waves generated by sudden vertical displacement of the seafloor during submarine megathrust earthquakes)
textbook_ref: William Lowrie (Fundamentals of Geophysics, Ch. 3, pp. 155-165); Edward A. Keller (Environmental Geology, Ch. 4)

topic: Deep Earth Seismology: P-Wave Shadow Zone Geometry
question: The Seismic shadow zone angle” _ a that exist from the epicenter is : =.
correct_text: 105° to 143° (Refraction of P-waves at the core-mantle boundary creates a distinct P-wave shadow zone on Earth's surface between 105 degrees and 143 degrees)
textbook_ref: William Lowrie (Fundamentals of Geophysics, 2nd Ed., Ch. 3, pp. 160-168); Stacey & Davis (Physics of the Earth)

topic: Elastic Wave Propagation: P-Wave Compressional Mechanics
question: Seismic P-waves can travel . through: :
correct_text: Crust, mantle and core (P-waves are longitudinal compressional waves supported by bulk incompressibility (K), allowing them to travel through solid crust, solid mantle, liquid outer core, and solid inner core)
textbook_ref: William Lowrie (Fundamentals of Geophysics, Ch. 3, pp. 135-145); Telford et al. (Applied Geophysics, Ch. 4)

topic: Inorganic Geochemistry: Rare Earth Elements (REE) Count
question: The total number of Rare Earth ; . Elements (REE) is :
correct_text: 17 (The Rare Earth Elements (IUPAC definition) comprise the 15 lanthanide elements (La to Lu, atomic numbers 57-71) plus Scandium (Sc, 21) and Yttrium (Y, 39))
textbook_ref: G.B. Haxel et al. (Rare Earth Elements—Critical Resources for High Technology, USGS Fact Sheet 087-02); Rollinson (Using Geochemical Data, Ch. 4)

topic: Planetary Interior: Geochemical Core Composition
question: The core of the earth is made up of: ;
correct_text: Nickel and iron (The Earth's core (core-mantle boundary to center) is primarily composed of an iron-nickel alloy (~85-90% Fe, ~5% Ni) plus light elements (S, O, Si))
textbook_ref: William Lowrie (Fundamentals of Geophysics, Ch. 3, pp. 170-178); Stacey & Davis (Physics of the Earth, Ch. 5)

topic: Industrial Minerals: Lapsa Buru Kyanite Deposit
question: Lapsa Buru mineral deposit is ; ee ‘famous for which mineral? oe a
correct_text: Kyanite (Lapsa Buru in the Singhbhum Shear Zone, Jharkhand hosts one of the world's largest massive aluminosilicate kyanite (Al2SiO5) deposits)
textbook_ref: Umeshwar Prasad (Economic Mineral Deposits, pp. 215-225); Krishnan (Geology of India, pp. 140-155)

topic: Water Resources Engineering: Bisalpur Dam on Banas River
question: Bilaspur Dam is constructed on | which river ? |
correct_text: Banas River (The Bisalpur gravity dam in Tonk district, Rajasthan is constructed on the Banas River to supply drinking water to Jaipur and Ajmer)

topic: Hydraulic Engineering: Hirakud Composite Embankment Dam
question: An example of Embankment dam | is: . ~ |

topic: Beach Sand Placers: Monazite Heavy Mineral Production
question: Monazite is produced most abundantly in: ° _ _
correct_text: Kerala (The Chavara/Manavalakurichi coastal beach placers of Kerala and Tamil Nadu are world-famous for monazite thorium-bearing radioactive sands)
textbook_ref: Umeshwar Prasad (Economic Mineral Deposits, pp. 235-248); Krishnan (Geology of India, pp. 280-295)

topic: Thermodynamics: Goldschmidt Mineralogical Phase Rule
question: Goldschmidt’s phase rule is. | 7 expressedas: 9° : |
correct_text: F = C + 2 - P (or P <= C) (At arbitrary pressure and temperature where variance F >= 2, the number of coexisting phases does not exceed components: P <= C; Gibbs rule is F = C + 2 - P)
textbook_ref: V.M. Goldschmidt (Die Gesetze der Gesteinsmetamorphose, 1912); John D. Winter (Principles of Igneous and Metamorphic Petrology, Ch. 24, pp. 505-520)

topic: Singhbhum Craton Geochronology: Singhbhum Granite Ages
question: The age of the Singhbhum Granite is:
correct_text: 3000-3400 Ma (Singhbhum Granite Phase II and Phase III plutons have yielded precise zircon U-Pb and Pb-Pb ages between ~3.3 Ga and ~3.4 Ga (3100-3400 Ma))
textbook_ref: K.S. Valdiya (The Making of India, Ch. 3, pp. 85-115); Mahadevan (Geology of Bihar and Jharkhand, Geological Society of India)

topic: Isotope Geochemistry: Radiogenic Lead Systematics
question: Which is the radiogenic isotope of Lead? ~ a 7
correct_text: Pb206 (or Pb208/Pb207) (206Pb (decay of 238U), 207Pb (decay of 235U), and 208Pb (decay of 232Th) are radiogenic isotopes; 204Pb is primordial/non-radiogenic)

topic: Mahanadi Gondwana Basin: Athgarh Sandstone Floral Assemblages
question: Athgarh(Odisha) is known for: | _ a) "Cretaceous fossils ; .
correct_text: Jurassic fossils (The Athgarh Sandstone of the Mahanadi Master Basin, Odisha yields Upper Gondwana Jurassic/Early Cretaceous plant fossils including Ptilophyllum)

topic: Pedology & Regolith: Lateritic Iron-Rich Soils

correct_text: Laterite (Intense tropical weathering leaches alkalis and silica, accumulating insoluble ferric oxides (goethite, hematite) forming brick-red lateritic soils)

topic: Rock Mechanics: In-Situ Modulus Plate Jacking Test
question: A static test conducted to know the ; in-situ deformation of rocks, is known as:
correct_text: Jack test (Plate jacking / flat jack tests apply static hydraulic loading against rock walls in exploration adits to measure in-situ modulus of deformation)

topic: Hydrogeology & Petrophysics: Fluid Transmission Capacity
question: The property of a rock to transmit fluids through it, is known as : .
correct_text: Permeability (Permeability (Darcy units) measures the capacity of a porous medium to transmit fluids under a hydraulic pressure gradient)
textbook_ref: D.K. Todd & L.W. Mays (Groundwater Hydrology, Ch. 3, pp. 55-75); H.M. Raghunath (Groundwater, Ch. 2)

topic: Solar System Geophysics: Terrestrial Planetary Densities
question: Which planet has highest density _ ; among these ? : a
correct_text: Earth (Earth is the densest planet in the solar system with a mean bulk density of 5.515 g/cm3; Mercury is 5.43, Venus 5.24, Mars 3.93)
textbook_ref: William Lowrie (Fundamentals of Geophysics, Ch. 2, pp. 50-65); Stacey & Davis (Physics of the Earth, Ch. 1)

topic: Feldspar Mineralogy: High-Temperature Disordered Sanidine
question: Which one is high temperature feldspar?
correct_text: Sanidine (Sanidine is the high-temperature, monoclinic disordered form of K-feldspar (KAlSi3O8) stable above ~500°C in rapidly quenched felsic volcanic rocks)
textbook_ref: Dexter Perkins (Mineralogy, 3rd Ed., Ch. 13, pp. 310-325); Cornelis Klein (Manual of Mineral Science, Ch. 19)

topic: Volcanology: Pyroclastic Density Current Deposits
question: Which one is a pyroclastic rock ?
correct_text: Ignimbrite (Ignimbrite is a poorly sorted pyroclastic rock formed by the consolidation and welding of pumice and ash from explosive pyroclastic density currents)
textbook_ref: Cas & Wright (Volcanic Successions, Ch. 9, pp. 235-265); John D. Winter (Principles of Igneous Petrology, Ch. 2)

topic: Plate Tectonics: Convergent Destructive Margins

correct_text: Converging plate boundary (Convergent margins (subduction zones) are termed destructive plate boundaries because oceanic lithosphere is consumed back into the mantle)
